subject: Physics
prompt: Principle of superposition states that resultant displacement is?
explain: Superposition: net displacement = vector (algebraic for 1-D) sum of each wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: End correction for a closed pipe (radius r) makes effective length?
explain: End correction ≈ 0.3d for closed end (one open end); accounts for antinode outside pipe.

subject: Physics
prompt: A wave y = A sin(ωt − kx): particle velocity at any point is?
explain: Particle velocity vₚ = ∂y/∂t = −(wave speed)×(∂y/∂x) for +x wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: Pitch of a sound is determined primarily by its?
explain: Pitch is the subjective perception corresponding to frequency of sound.

subject: Physics
prompt: Loudness of sound is determined primarily by its?
explain: Loudness depends on intensity which depends on amplitude squared.

subject: Physics
prompt: Quality (timbre) of sound depends on?
explain: Timbre distinguishes sounds of same pitch/loudness via their harmonic content.

subject: Physics
prompt: Velocity of sound is maximum in which medium?
explain: Solids have highest elasticity; v_solid > v_liquid > v_gas.

subject: Physics
prompt: Frequency of beats does NOT depend on?
explain: Beat frequency = |f₁−f₂|; amplitudes affect loudness of beats, not frequency.

subject: Physics
prompt: Group velocity equals phase velocity when dispersion is?
explain: No dispersion means dv_p/dλ = 0, so group velocity = phase velocity.

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of sound in air is approximately (at 0°C)?
explain: Standard value of speed of sound in air at 0°C is ~332 m/s.

subject: Physics
prompt: Slope of displacement-distance graph of a wave gives?
explain: ∂y/∂x is the strain (longitudinal compression/rarefaction) at a point.

subject: Physics
prompt: A tuning fork of 300 Hz moves toward a wall at 10 m/s (v=340 m/s). Beat freq heard?
explain: Reflected freq ≈ 300×(340+10)/(340−10)≈318 Hz; beats ≈ 18 Hz.

subject: Physics
prompt: Melde's experiment: tension T, loops n. Relation between n and T?
explain: Frequency f fixed by fork; f = (n/2L)√(T/μ) → n ∝ 1/√T.

subject: Physics
prompt: Doppler effect is observed when source AND observer are both stationary but medium moves?
explain: If medium moves, the effective v changes; observed frequency remains unchanged.

subject: Physics
prompt: For transverse wave on string, maximum particle speed equals wave speed when?
explain: Max particle speed vₚ_max = Aω; equals wave speed v when Aω = v.

subject: Physics
prompt: Energy of a standing wave compared to the two constituent travelling waves?
explain: Standing wave energy equals the sum of energies of the two constituent waves.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which property of sound corresponds to the 'waveform' of the wave?
explain: Quality/timbre depends on the mixture of harmonics, i.e., the waveform shape.

subject: Physics
prompt: Resonance column: end correction 'e' is expressed in terms of pipe radius r as?
explain: End correction for open end of a pipe is approximately 0.6r (or 0.3d) for radius r.

subject: Physics
prompt: The number of antinodes in nth harmonic of an open pipe is?
explain: Open pipe nth harmonic has n antinodes and (n+1) nodes including displacement nodes.

subject: Physics
prompt: Melde's law: frequency of vibration f ∝ √T (T = tension). So n ∝ ?
explain: Melde's law: n√T = const, so number of loops n ∝ 1/√T for fixed frequency source.

subject: Physics
prompt: Energy stored in a standing wave compared to a single progressive wave of same amplitude?
explain: Standing wave = superposition of 2 progressive waves; total energy is double one wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: The phenomenon of resonance occurs when applied frequency equals the body's?
explain: Resonance: maximum energy transfer when driving frequency matches natural frequency of system.

subject: Physics
prompt: Loudness is measured in which unit?
explain: Sound level (loudness) is measured in decibels (dB).

subject: Physics
prompt: In resonance column, end correction e in terms of radius r is?
explain: Empirically, end correction e ≈ 0.6r where r is the radius of the pipe.

subject: Physics
prompt: Wavelength of sound in a medium of density ρ, bulk modulus B, frequency f?
explain: v = √(B/ρ) and λ = v/f, so λ = (1/f)√(B/ρ).

subject: Physics
prompt: Particle velocity (vₚ) and wave velocity (v) are related by (for y = A sin(ωt−kx))?
explain: ∂y/∂t = −v·∂y/∂x; particle velocity equals −v times slope of wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: Melde's law: string of length L, tension T. Number of loops n ∝ ?
explain: f = (n/2L)√(T/μ); for constant f and L, n ∝ 1/√T.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a progressive wave, energy is transported. For a standing wave, energy transported is?
explain: In a standing wave, equal energy flows in +x and −x; net energy transport is zero.

subject: Physics
prompt: Sound wave is a longitudinal wave. The compressions and rarefactions travel at?
explain: Compressions and rarefactions propagate at the speed of sound in the medium.

subject: Physics
prompt: If a pipe open at both ends is cut in half, its fundamental frequency?
explain: f = v/2L; halving L doubles the fundamental frequency.

subject: Physics
prompt: Frequency of 1st overtone of open pipe vs 1st overtone of closed pipe (same length L)?
explain: Open 1st overtone = v/L; closed 1st overtone = 3v/4L; ratio = 4/3.

subject: Physics
prompt: A transverse wave travels on a string. Particle at crest has velocity?
explain: At crest (antinode position for progressive wave), displacement is max so particle velocity = 0.

subject: Physics
prompt: The wave speed on a string depends on which property of the medium?
explain: v = √(T/μ): speed depends on tension T and linear mass density μ of the string.

subject: Physics
prompt: Fundamental frequency of open pipe of length L?
explain: Open pipe has antinodes at both ends; fundamental wavelength = 2L, so f = v/2L.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a string of length L fixed at both ends, fundamental wavelength is?
explain: Fundamental mode has one antinode; both ends are nodes, so λ₁ = 2L.

subject: Physics
prompt: Standing wave: distance between two consecutive antinodes is?
explain: Consecutive antinodes (or nodes) are always separated by half a wavelength.

subject: Physics
prompt: In resonance column (open pipe), 1st resonance at L₁, 2nd at L₂. λ =?
explain: Successive resonances in open pipe differ by λ/2, so λ = 2(L₂ − L₁).

subject: Physics
prompt: What is the phase difference between displacement and pressure wave in sound?
explain: Pressure wave leads displacement wave by π/2 (90°) in a sound wave.

subject: Physics
prompt: If amplitude doubles, intensity of a wave changes by factor?
explain: Intensity ∝ A², so doubling amplitude quadruples the intensity.

subject: Physics
prompt: For open pipe, ratio of frequencies of 1st, 2nd, 3rd harmonics is?
explain: Open pipe supports all harmonics; frequencies are f, 2f, 3f … giving 1:2:3.

subject: Physics
prompt: Closed pipe: ratio of 1st, 2nd, 3rd harmonics (odd only) is?
explain: Closed pipe supports only odd harmonics: f, 3f, 5f … ratio 1:3:5.

subject: Physics
prompt: Wave y = A sin(ωt − kx). Slope of y-x graph (∂y/∂x) equals?
explain: Differentiating y w.r.t. x gives ∂y/∂x = −Ak cos(ωt − kx).

subject: Physics
prompt: Relation: particle velocity vₚ = −v × (∂y/∂x). Here v is?
explain: For a progressive wave, particle velocity = −(wave speed) × slope of y-x curve.

subject: Physics
prompt: For a string vibrating in nth mode, number of nodes (incl. ends) is?
explain: nth harmonic has n loops, n−1 internal nodes plus 2 endpoints = n+1 nodes total.

subject: Physics
prompt: Effect of humidity on speed of sound: moist air has speed?
explain: Moist air has lower density (water vapour lighter than N₂/O₂), so v = √(γP/ρ) increases.

subject: Physics
prompt: Which quantity does NOT change when sound passes from air to water?
explain: Frequency is determined by source and remains unchanged on crossing media boundary.

subject: Physics
prompt: Sound intensity level increases by 3 dB. Intensity changes by factor?
explain: 10 log(I₂/I₁) = 3 ⟹ I₂/I₁ = 10^0.3 ≈ 2; intensity approximately doubles.

subject: Physics
prompt: The maximum particle speed in a wave y = A sin(ωt−kx) is?
explain: Particle velocity = ∂y/∂t = Aω cos(ωt−kx); maximum value = Aω.

subject: Physics
prompt: A sound wave of frequency f has speed v in air. Its wavelength λ =?
explain: Basic wave relation: v = fλ, so λ = v/f.

subject: Physics
prompt: In Melde's experiment, n loops form with tension T. If T becomes 4T, loops become?
explain: n ∝ 1/√T; quadrupling T halves n: new loops = n/2.

subject: Physics
prompt: Standing wave y = 2A sin(kx)cos(ωt): amplitude at x = λ/6 is?
explain: Amplitude = 2A sin(kx); at x=λ/6, kx = π/3, so amplitude = 2A·(√3/2) = A√3.

subject: Physics
prompt: Ratio of speed of sound in oxygen to nitrogen at same temperature (γ same)?
explain: v ∝ √(γRT/M); same γ and T, so v_O₂/v_N₂ = √(M_N₂/M_O₂) = √(28/32).

subject: Physics
prompt: For a closed organ pipe, the 1st overtone frequency compared to fundamental?
explain: Closed pipe: 1st overtone is 3rd harmonic = 3f₀ (only odd harmonics exist).

subject: Physics
prompt: Two waves I₁ = I, I₂ = 4I interfere. Maximum intensity is?
explain: Iₘₐₓ = (√I + 2√I)² = (3√I)² = 9I.

subject: Physics
prompt: Speed of sound in ideal gas: v ∝ T^n. Value of n is?
explain: v = √(γRT/M) ∝ T^(1/2); speed of sound is proportional to square root of absolute temperature.
